steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Non-verbal communication (NVC) conveys meaning without words: body language (posture, gestures), facial expressions (emotions), eye contact (interest, honesty), proxemics (use of personal space), and paralinguistics (tone, pitch, speed of voice).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Facial expressions: Ekman found six basic emotions expressed universally across cultures - happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, disgust. This suggests facial expressions are innate (supporting nature). However, display rules (cultural rules about when to show emotions) affect how freely people express them.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Eye contact: signals interest and attention. Too little suggests dishonesty or disinterest; too much can feel threatening. Cultural differences: in some cultures, direct eye contact with authority is respectful; in others, it is rude.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Proxemics (Hall): four zones of personal space - intimate (0-0.5m, close relationships), personal (0.5-1.2m, friends), social (1.2-3.6m, acquaintances), public (3.6m+, strangers). Violating personal space causes discomfort.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the key types of non-verbal communication and explain how each conveys meaning. | Evaluate whether facial expressions are universal or culturally specific, using research evidence. | Explain how proxemics can affect social interactions, referring to Hall's zones of personal space.
